content: This medication belongs to a class of drugs called diuretics, or water pills. It works by helping the kidneys eliminate excess water and sodium through urine while minimizing the loss of potassium. Triamterene and hydrochlorothiazide are available in capsule and tablet forms, taken orally, usually once daily. It is important to take this medication at the same time each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Do not take more or less of the medication or take it more frequently than prescribed. Continue taking it even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other purposes. If you have questions about its use, ask your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before starting triamterene and hydrochlorothiazide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to triamterene, hydrochlorothiazide, sulfonamide-derived medications (sulfa drugs), or any other substances. Do not take this medication if you are already taking amiloride, spironolactone, or other drugs containing triamterene. Provide your doctor with a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are using or plan to use. This includes amphotericin B, ACE inhibitors (e.g., benazepril, captopril, enalapril), anticoagulants like warfarin, barbiturates, digoxin, laxatives, lithium, diabetes medications, gout medications, NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen), oral steroids, potassium supplements, and others. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have a history of kidney stones, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), diabetes, gout, or thyroid, heart, kidney, or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, let your doctor know. Do not breastfeed while taking this medication. If you become pregnant while on this medication, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking triamterene and hydrochlorothiazide. Be aware that this medication may cause dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting, especially when standing up too quickly from a lying position. This is more likely when you first start taking the medication and may be worsened by alcohol consumption. To minimize this effect, rise slowly from bed, allowing your feet to rest on the floor for a few minutes before standing. Follow your doctor’s dietary recommendations, which may include a low-sodium diet. Avoid potassium-containing salt substitutes while taking this medication. Discuss with your doctor the appropriate amount of potassium-rich foods, such as bananas, prunes, raisins, and orange juice, that you can include in your diet. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. This medication may cause side effects. Minor side effects include gas, frequent urination, dizziness, and headache. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Serious side effects require immediate medical attention. These include rash or hives, difficulty breathing or swallowing, upper stomach pain, swelling or tenderness in the stomach area, nausea, vomiting, fever, rapid heartbeat, extreme fatigue, unusual bruising or bleeding, loss of appetite, yellowing of the skin or eyes, flu-like symptoms, muscle weakness or cramps, numbness or tingling sensations, inability to move limbs, slow or irregular heartbeat, severe dry mouth, intense thirst, muscle pain or fatigue, and decreased urination. If you experience any of these, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include increased urination, nausea, vomiting, weakness, fatigue, and fever. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as regular tests may be required to monitor your response to the medication. Inform your doctor and lab personnel that you are taking triamterene and hydrochlorothiazide before undergoing any tests. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. This medication is sold under the brand names Dyazide® and Maxzide®.
